title: Route policy evaluation: quantization enablement toggle + precedence + routing/fallback integration tests
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Context
- Quantization Profile Library is opt-in and must be enableable per API route/workload.
- This ticket adds policy-evaluation support (and tests) so Smart Routing can make a deterministic decision: attempt quantized path vs baseline.

Problem
- Today routing/policy has no first-class concept of “quantization enabled for this route”, and no precedence rules across org/customer/route.
- We also need canary percent gating to safely roll out quantization within a route.

Goal
- Extend policy engine evaluation to produce an effective QuantizationPolicy for each request.
- Implement precedence rules (org default -> customer override -> route override) with explicit enable/disable.
- Add integration tests that cover: enablement + canary selection + fallback behavior when quantization is incompatible/unavailable.

Non-goals (for this ticket)
- Runtime profile lookup/compatibility implementation (covered in ENG-18437).
- Console UX and API endpoints for editing config (covered elsewhere; this ticket consumes the resolved config as input).

Proposed policy model (evaluated per request)
- Inputs:
  - org_quantization_default: {enabled|disabled|unset}
  - customer_quantization_override: {enabled|disabled|unset}
  - route_quantization_setting: {enabled|disabled|unset, canary_percent (0-100), allow_profile_families (optional)}
  - request attributes: org_id, customer_id, route_id, model, region, request_id/trace_id
  - feature flags: quant_profiles_route_toggle (global), quant_profiles_canary_toggle (global)
- Output:
  - quantization_attempt: {true|false}
  - quantization_reason: enum string (e.g., disabled_by_route, disabled_by_customer, disabled_by_org_default, canary_miss, global_flag_off, enabled)
  - canary_bucket: stable integer 0-99 (if canary enabled)

Precedence rules (explicit)
1) Global flag off => quantization_attempt=false (reason=global_flag_off)
2) If route setting explicitly disabled => false (reason=disabled_by_route)
3) Else if customer override explicitly disabled => false (reason=disabled_by_customer)
4) Else if route setting explicitly enabled => evaluate canary gate and decide
5) Else if customer override explicitly enabled => evaluate canary gate and decide
6) Else if org default explicitly enabled => evaluate canary gate and decide
7) Else => false (reason=unset_default)

Canary selection
- Deterministic bucketing to avoid per-request jitter:
  - bucket = hash64(org_id, customer_id, route_id, request_id_or_trace_id) % 100
  - quantization_attempt=true iff bucket < canary_percent
- If canary feature flag off, treat canary_percent as 100 when enabled (i.e., enabled => attempt for all traffic).

Interaction with fallback (contract with runtime/routing)
- Policy engine only decides “attempt quantized path”. Runtime/resolver may still refuse due to incompatibility/missing profile.
- Router must treat runtime refusal as a soft failure and proceed baseline, while preserving observability tags.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Policy engine exports an evaluated QuantizationPolicy attached to routing context.
- [x] Precedence rules above implemented and covered by unit tests.
- [x] Canary bucketing stable and covered by tests (same inputs -> same bucket).
- [x] Integration tests:
  - (a) Quantization enabled at route (100%) => router attempts quantized; if resolver returns compatible profile => quantized path chosen.
  - (b) Quantization enabled at customer but route disables => baseline chosen.
  - (c) Quantization enabled but resolver returns incompatibility => baseline chosen and reason surfaced in metrics/log context.
  - (d) Canary 10% => approximately correct selection in deterministic test harness (bucket boundary conditions).
- [x] Backwards-compatible defaults: if config missing/unknown => baseline.
- [x] Feature-flag guarded end-to-end (safe to deploy with flag off).

Implementation notes
- Add a QuantizationPolicy struct in policy-engine package with minimal fields to avoid coupling to registry schema.
- Avoid throwing hard errors for invalid canary_percent; clamp to [0,100] and emit config_validation warning metric (this avoids taking down routing for a bad config write).
- Ensure evaluation runs before routing fallback selection so fallback can observe the attempt decision.

Testing approach
- Unit tests in policy-engine:
  - precedence matrix
  - canary bucketing determinism
  - canary percent edge cases (0, 100, negative, >100)
- Integration tests in routing service:
  - use a stub resolver to return (compatible profile) vs (incompatible) without requiring registry.
  - assert routing decision + emitted context tags.

Links
- Design intent: route-scoped opt-in + canary + fast rollback (see ADR in Confluence; referenced in team discussions)
- Related work:
  - ENG-18420: profile schema/registry storage
  - ENG-18437: runtime fetch/cache/compat checks
comments:
2025-02-06 — Jordan Lee (creator)
We need to make sure precedence is explicit and matches what Platform/Console will expose. I’d like route disable to win over customer enable (so a team can protect a sensitive route like JSON-mode). Please confirm with Product but I think that’s the safest default.

Also: canary bucketing should not depend on any mutable headers; use request_id or trace_id (stable) and include route_id to avoid cross-route correlation.

2025-02-10 — Mina Haddad
+1 on route disable winning. For canary hash, include org_id/customer_id/route_id to avoid collisions across tenants.

One more request: surface an explicit reason string in routing context so runtime + telemetry can tag ‘canary_miss’ vs ‘disabled_by_route’ etc. That’s going to matter for support/debugging.

2025-02-12 — Benji Okafor (assignee)
Drafted policy evaluation function with the precedence matrix from description. Plan:
1) Implement QuantizationPolicy output + wire into routing context
2) Unit test matrix (table-driven)
3) Add integration test harness with stub resolver (compatible/incompatible)

Open question: If customer override is ‘enabled’ but doesn’t specify canary_percent, do we inherit route canary? Proposal: route canary applies only when route explicitly enables; otherwise use customer-level canary (default 100).

2025-02-13 — Paula Mendes
Re: canary defaults: for MVP please keep it simple: canary_percent lives at route-level. If enablement comes from org/customer, treat as 100% unless route specifies canary. (We can add customer-level canary later.)

2025-02-18 — Benji Okafor
Implemented per-request canary bucketing using (org_id, customer_id, route_id, trace_id) and plumbed QuantizationPolicy into RouterContext.

Unit tests added for:
- precedence (route/customer/org)
- percent edge cases (clamp)
- deterministic hashing

Next: routing integration tests. Need a stub that mimics resolver returning ‘no compatible profile’ so we assert baseline fallback + tags.

2025-02-24 — Ravi Menon
Please ensure ‘global flag off’ is evaluated first. We’ve had issues where config evaluation ran before feature-flag checks and we still emitted “enabled” tags even though feature was disabled. Those tags cause confusion.

Also note: we need a separate boolean for “attempted quantization” vs “actually ran quantized path” (runtime will own the latter).

2025-02-27 — Benji Okafor
Integration tests landed:
- enabled route -> attempts quantized; stub resolver returns compatible -> selects quantized path
- enabled route -> stub resolver returns incompatible -> selects baseline, logs reason ‘profile_incompatible’ while policy reason stays ‘enabled’
- route disabled overrides customer enabled -> baseline
- canary boundary test: bucket 9 with 10% => enabled; bucket 10 with 10% => disabled

Wiring: RouterContext now carries quantization_attempt + policy_reason. Runtime execution path will add execution_mode later (baseline/quantized).

Ready for review.

2025-03-04 — Jordan Lee
Merged and verified in staging with feature flag off: no behavior change, only code path available. With flag on and a test config, routing context shows expected policy_reason + canary_miss. Marking Done.
